pass_b_english: After the mystery had been fully passed through in the economy of the flesh, one might ask how the one who is about to come would be called. For he has set before us the first man and recalled the times of the transgression, declaring that the one who would come after them and be the last is Adam, whom he has named the Christ. He was indeed foreordained according to the will and foreknowledge of God the Father as savior and redeemer, yet he revealed himself in his own times, as the ruler had willed.

These are they who stand at the end, and as it were, upon the western borders of the present age. Thus, having established the second as a type of the first, he not only tests the listener but speaks as if by a mark and interrogation, saying what follows. Not as the transgression, so also the gift? For just as one might say we are condemned to death through the transgression in Adam—this suffering affecting the whole of human nature in him—and for he was the first-fruit of the race, again in Christ we sprout forth into life.

Adam was a type of the one who was to come, that is, Christ, through the clumsiness of those who preceded, bringing in to us the grace of equal sharing. Therefore, he says: 'Did I miss the truth by saying this? Have I been carried outside the reasonable? Not as the transgression, so also the gift? But death prevailed through one, and life is made ineffective through one. And yet, how could that not be true to say? For if by the transgression of the one man the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift by grace through the one man Jesus Christ abound to the many.'
